claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, let me ask: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you tell me:
- How many children you have
- Their ages
- Their names (so I can assess eligibility for each child individually)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child. His name is Alex and he's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 19 years old, I need to ask some important follow-up questions to assess eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

(Approved education or training typically includes things like A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing an apprenticeship in Dundee.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify what type of apprenticeship Alex is doing, as this affects eligibility.

**Is Alex doing an apprenticeship in England, or is this a different type of apprenticeship program in Scotland?**

This is important because the rules state that Child Benefit stops if a child starts an apprenticeship in England, but apprenticeships in Scotland may be treated differently.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's in Scotland - he's doing his apprenticeship in Dundee, Scotland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Now I need to ask a few more questions about your situation:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great. Now I need to ask:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards his upkeep?** 

(This could include things like food, clothes, accommodation costs, or pocket money)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex working for 24 hours or more per week in paid work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working separately - he's just doing his apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Alex is 19 years old and lives with you, which means you're responsible for him. Although he's doing an apprenticeship, it's in Scotland, not England. The rules specifically state that Child Benefit stops if a child starts an apprenticeship in England, but Scottish apprenticeships are treated differently and count as approved education or training. Since Alex is under 20, not working 24+ hours per week in separate paid employment, and not claiming benefits in his own right, you qualify for Child Benefit.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator to work out if this applies to you.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
